site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full booking system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The core booking funnel is understandable and mostly works end to end: search, results, detail, room selection, and the reservation form all communicate a coherent path, with clear policy context and visible confirmation-style feedback in several places. The biggest UX issues are on mobile, where compact controls, small touch targets, and horizontal overflow make key pages harder to scan and operate. There are also a few trust and clarity gaps around booking completion and form labeling, plus at least one support/search path that appears to accept input without giving clear result feedback. Important adjacent areas like airport taxis and flights were covered, but some business-line link coverage remains limited relative to the full surface area.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the primary hotel booking funnel from home search through Tokyo/Shinjuku listings, hotel detail, room selection, reservation, and confirmation, while also validating adjacent flows such as sign-in/register, help, trips management, and related business-line pages.
exploration_plan.summary: Start with the main stay-search path on index.html and drive into the Tokyo/Shinjuku listing pages to validate search, filters, sort/map entry points, and property navigation. Then follow at least one full property journey through hotel detail, reviews, room selection, reservation, and confirmation, checking that back links and cross-links to trips/help remain coherent. After the core funnel, sweep the adjacent pages and business-line pages to confirm secondary flows, and repeat critical interactions on mobile to surface tap-target and label issues already hinted by prescan warnings.
assumptions: The checkout flow is intentionally simplified and may not require external services or real form submission; success is represented by navigating between static pages.
Search and booking controls on the listings and booking pages are expected to move between prewired states rather than perform live filtering or network-backed search.
The Tokyo and Shinjuku pages are the primary listing entry points, with Park Hyatt Tokyo and Shinjuku Granbell Hotel as the most important property-detail anchors.
Multiple pages share the same header navigation, so one or two representative checks are sufficient to validate global nav behavior.
Mobile findings will likely be mostly accessibility/tap-target issues rather than functional breakage, based on the prescan's repeated small-tap-target warnings.
risk_hotspots: index.html search bar inputs and the Search button leading into tokyo.html
tokyo.html and shinjuku.html filter-heavy sidebars with many inputs and the 'No properties match your filters' empty state
hotel-detail.html / hotel-detail-granbell.html review links, reserve CTA, and breadcrumb/back navigation
reviews.html sorting and segment filters (All, Couples, Families, Solo travellers, Business)
room-selection.html 'Continue to booking details' CTA and price-summary consistency
reservation.html multi-field guest details form, country selector, guest-for toggles, and special requests textarea
confirmation.html links to My trips, Manage your booking, Back to home, and downstream travel-related cross-sells
my-trips.html action buttons for Cancel booking, Modify dates, Write a review, and Book again
help.html support search plus Chat with us / Call us buttons
signin.html and register.html authentication entry forms with multiple sign-up methods
all pages with repeated small tap-target warnings in mobile viewport, especially top nav and footer links

phases.title: Home search and entry navigation
phases.objective: Validate the start page search experience and the main entry points into the booking funnel and adjacent business areas.
key_checks: Enter or confirm Tokyo as the destination, inspect the check-in/check-out and guest fields, and use Search to reach tokyo.html.
Open at least one trending destination and one footer or header navigation item to confirm the global nav works.
Check that Sign in, Register, List your property, Flights, Car rentals, Attractions, and Airport taxis are reachable from the homepage.
exit_criteria: Search successfully navigates to a listing page.
At least two non-search nav links have been exercised.
No unexpected console or navigation errors appear from the home entry path.

phases.title: Listing pages and filter behavior
phases.objective: Validate the Tokyo and Shinjuku result pages, including search criteria persistence, filter panels, sorting, and empty-state handling.
key_checks: Inspect the visible filter groups on both pages: budget, popular filters, star rating, neighbourhood, property type, and review score.
Toggle a representative filter or sort option and verify the property list/state changes or the no-results message appears appropriately.
Use the property cards and location/breadcrumb links to open a hotel detail page.
Verify the show-on-map or map-related entry point if present without assuming a full map experience.
exit_criteria: At least one filter/sort interaction has been tested on each or representative listing page.
A property card has been opened into the detail flow.

phases.title: Hotel detail and social proof
phases.objective: Check property detail content, review surfaces, breadcrumb/back links, and reserve-related calls to action for the main hotel path.
key_checks: From Park Hyatt Tokyo, validate the property summary, location, review score, and 'Reserve' or equivalent CTA.
Open guest reviews and test sort/filter controls such as Most relevant, Most recent, and audience segments.
Visit the alternate hotel detail page for Shinjuku Granbell Hotel to compare structure and breadcrumb behavior.
Confirm cross-links from detail pages to home, Tokyo, Shinjuku, and reviews behave consistently.
exit_criteria: At least one hotel detail page and the reviews page are fully exercised.
The reserve/review-related path is confirmed navigable.
Breadcrumb or back navigation does not trap the user.

phases.title: Room selection and booking checkout
phases.objective: Validate the core booking handoff from room selection to reservation details and the final confirmation state.
key_checks: Inspect the selected room, price summary, cancellation policy, and 'Continue to booking details' CTA on room-selection.html.
Complete or partially complete the reservation form, including name, email, country/region, phone, booking-for toggles, and special requests.
Check the arrival/payment/cancellation information blocks for clarity and consistency.
Confirm that confirmation.html shows booking status, booking reference, trip summary, and links to My trips / Manage your booking / Back to home.
exit_criteria: The flow reaches the confirmation page.
Booking reference and trip details are visible on confirmation.
Form fields and booking policy text have been checked for obvious usability issues.

phases.title: Post-booking management and support
phases.objective: Validate account/trips/support recovery paths that surround the booking journey.
key_checks: Open My trips and test tabs or segment controls like Upcoming, Completed, and Cancelled.
Exercise booking actions such as View details, Cancel booking, Modify dates, Write a review, and Book again.
Use Help Center search plus Chat with us / Call us buttons to confirm support entry points.
Check Sign in and Register forms for field presence, submit buttons, and alternate login/sign-up methods.
exit_criteria: Help and auth entry points are verified.
No dead-end or broken recovery path is encountered.

phases.title: Adjacent business-line pages and mobile sanity pass
phases.objective: Cover the non-stays pages and repeat critical interactions at mobile viewport to catch layout/tap-target regressions.
key_checks: On each adjacent page, inspect the primary search form or promotion module and one representative CTA such as Search, Book, View deal, or Get started now.
Confirm header navigation consistency across these pages, especially Flights/Car rentals/Attractions/Airport taxis and Sign in.
Repeat the most important booking-flow checks on mobile viewport: homepage search, one listing page filter interaction, hotel reserve path, and reservation form usability.
Record whether the known small tap targets become materially problematic on mobile.
exit_criteria: All known HTML pages have been visited at least once.
Key adjacent pages each have at least one meaningful interaction tested.
Critical booking-path checks have been repeated in mobile viewport.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all known HTML pages in the prescan, with full-depth coverage on the booking funnel pages and at least one interaction on each adjacent/business/support page.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on the core funnel pages: search fields, filters, sort/filter chips, property/detail links, reserve CTA, booking form fields, trip-management actions, and support/auth entry points.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the homepage search, one listing filter or sort interaction, one hotel-detail reserve path, and the reservation form on mobile viewport, focusing on tap-targets and missing-label issues.

notes: Prescan shows no console or network errors, so prioritization should be on UX integrity, navigation completeness, and mobile accessibility rather than fault recovery.
Repeated small tap-target warnings across header/footer and page-level CTAs are a strong signal to inspect touch usability in mobile mode.

findings.user_goal: Book or refine travel options on a phone without accidental taps or layout problems
findings.problem: Several key pages overflow horizontally on mobile and compress important controls into cramped areas, making the interface harder to scan and operate. The Tokyo results page showed content wider than the 390px viewport, and the flights page showed similar overflow with multiple undersized controls.
findings.evidence: Mobile observations reported horizontal overflow on tokyo.html (631px and later 813px content vs 390px viewport) and on flights.html (631px vs 390px). Layout warnings also flagged many small tap targets below 44px, including header links, radio buttons, and the JPY button.
findings.why_it_matters: On a phone, users may miss controls, mis-tap filters, or have to pan around to understand the page, which directly hurts booking and comparison tasks.
findings.suggestion: Rework the mobile layout to stack filters and header actions vertically, prevent horizontal overflow, and enlarge interactive targets to at least 44px with more spacing between controls.

findings.user_goal: Understand and complete booking and search forms confidently
findings.problem: Several form controls lack labels or accessible names, which makes their purpose ambiguous and reduces accessibility. This affects search inputs and select controls across the funnel, including the Tokyo destination field, the reservation country/region select, and the flights cabin-class select.
findings.evidence: DOM/observation warnings noted missing labels or placeholders on tokyo.html destination input, reservation.html country/region select, and flights.html cabin-class select. The flights select was operable, but only its own displayed value changed; the purpose was still unclear from labeling.
findings.why_it_matters: Unlabeled fields are harder to understand for all users and especially problematic for screen-reader and mobile users, increasing errors and abandonment risk.
findings.suggestion: Add persistent visible labels plus accessible names for every form control, and avoid relying on placeholder text alone for meaning.

findings.user_goal: Know whether a booking action succeeded and what happens next
findings.problem: The final booking submission appears blocked without clear in-page resolution: the 'Complete booking' button was disabled and clicking it timed out, with no visible explanation of what remained missing or how to proceed.
findings.evidence: A click on reservation.html 'Complete booking' failed because the button was disabled. The timeout log showed the control remained non-enabled, and no success state or error message was surfaced in the tested interaction.
findings.why_it_matters: When a primary CTA is disabled without obvious reason, users can feel stuck at the last step of checkout and may not know which field or condition is preventing completion.
findings.suggestion: Show an inline checklist or error summary explaining exactly what is missing to enable booking, and make the CTA state tied to visible completion cues.

findings.user_goal: Refine search or support queries and know that the system responded
findings.problem: The help search accepts text, but submitting the search produced no visible result state, navigation, or no-results feedback, so users cannot tell whether their query was processed.
findings.evidence: On help.html, typing 'booking change fees' left the query visible in the field, and clicking Search produced no visible change in content or URL. The page remained on the same help center view.
findings.why_it_matters: Support is a recovery path; if search feels inert, users may assume the tool is broken and give up before finding help.
findings.suggestion: After search, show results, a loading state, or a clear empty/no-results message so users get immediate confirmation that the query was handled.

findings.user_goal: Move between travel products and account/support areas quickly
findings.problem: Cross-product navigation is present, but many header and footer links are undersized on mobile, which makes the shared navigation feel fragile and easy to mis-tap.
findings.evidence: Mobile observations repeatedly flagged small tap targets in the header across tokyo.html and flights.html, and in the footer/support region on flights.html and airport-taxis.html. Examples include Stays, Flights, JPY, Sign in, and footer links like Deals.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot reliably hit global navigation, they lose a key way to recover, compare products, or switch tasks mid-flow.
findings.suggestion: Increase tap target size and spacing for global nav and footer links, and consider collapsing less critical links into a menu on small screens.

findings.user_goal: Recognize what each control does in booking and flight searches
findings.problem: Several controls present as icon-only or minimally explained actions, which adds ambiguity in dense booking headers and search strips.
findings.evidence: The flights mobile observation shows a row of icons for origin/destination/date/passenger search fields, and the page also includes a cabin-class select with no label. On mobile, the meaning of the icons is not self-evident without surrounding context.
findings.why_it_matters: Icon-heavy controls can be efficient for experienced users but are easy to misread for first-time or hurried users, especially when space is already tight.
findings.suggestion: Pair icons with concise text labels or helper text, particularly for the search strip and any non-obvious selectors.

findings.user_goal: Finish booking without uncertainty at the last step
findings.problem: The reservation step communicates required fields well, but the transition from filled inputs to an enabled booking CTA was not visible, leaving the completion state uncertain.
findings.evidence: The reservation page clearly states 'Almost done! Just fill in the * required info,' and required fields are visible. Typed first and last names were accepted, but the booking CTA remained in its gated state during the test, with no visible progression indicator.
findings.why_it_matters: Users need a clear sense of progress in checkout; otherwise they may not know whether they are close to completion or whether more work is required.
findings.suggestion: Add a completion checklist or dynamic progress indicator that updates as fields are filled and explains when the final booking button becomes available.

findings.user_goal: Use results and filters confidently on mobile
findings.problem: Some actionable items are visually too small to feel comfortably tappable, even when they work correctly.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout warnings and observations flagged 13x13 radio buttons, 16x16 checkboxes, and 71x32 Select buttons on flights.html and tokyo.html, while interactions still succeeded.
findings.why_it_matters: Tiny controls increase the chance of missed taps and frustration, especially on dense comparison pages where users adjust filters repeatedly.
findings.suggestion: Enlarge checkboxes, radios, and select-trigger affordances, and provide more vertical spacing between adjacent controls.

findings.user_goal: Feel confident that actions are being registered
findings.problem: Some interactions provide only subtle state changes, which may be easy to miss even when the control works.
findings.evidence: Changing the flights cabin-class select on mobile updated from Economy to Premium Economy, but there was no obvious confirmation beyond the select’s displayed value. By contrast, other actions used clearer toasts or chip updates.
findings.why_it_matters: When feedback is understated, users may repeat actions, doubt whether a change stuck, or miss the effect of an important refinement.
findings.suggestion: Use a brief inline confirmation or visibly highlight the changed filter so the state shift is unmistakable.

gaps: Only directly exercised 7% of visible interactive feature signatures.
5 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
